name: a_geopolitics_trade
prompt:
Search the web now. You are a financial fact extractor for a US-equity pre-market brief.
Brief date: Friday October 16, 2026. Topic: Geopolitics & trade.

Window: Thursday October 15, 2026 regular session (9:30-16:00 ET) through Friday October 16, 2026 02:03 ET, including after-hours, overnight and pre-market news. Anything published after 02:03 ET on Friday October 16, 2026 is out of scope.

FIND
US-China relations (summits, trade truce, tariffs, export controls, chip rules, restrictions on foreign-made products or components — with the US stocks that benefit or lose), Iran / Middle East / Strait of Hormuz, Russia-Ukraine, sanctions — named officials, dates, terms, deadlines; latest status as of the cutoff.

Run multiple searches with different phrasings and dates. Prefer primary sources and wire services
(Reuters, Bloomberg, AP, CNBC, WSJ, MarketWatch, Barron's, Investopedia, company press releases, SEC
EDGAR, BLS/BEA/Census/Fed releases, FDA). For every item give the latest status as of the cutoff.

OUTPUT (markdown; no intro or conclusion). Group by ticker or topic:

## TICKER or Topic `[Category]`
- fact (source)

Category: pick from AI Compute · Memory & Interconnect · Optical & Photonics · Chip Equipment · Fab & Foundry · Wireless & Mobile · Analog & Mixed-Signal · Power & Wide-Bandgap · Test & Advanced Packaging · Specialty Materials & IP Licensing · Quantum Computing · EdgeAI · Semiconductors · AI Infrastructure · Software & SaaS · Internet & Platforms · Communications & Networking, or Macro / Commodities / Geopolitics / Crypto / Calendar /
Pharma / Energy / Retail, or a concise sector name. Bold tickers.

RULES
- Facts only. Every bullet has a specific number, name, or date. No bullet without a data point.
- End every bullet with the named source and publish time if known: (Reuters, Sep 24 07:12 ET).
  Convert every time to ET (ET = GMT-4 / UTC-4 in EDT; 09:59 GMT = 05:59 ET) before judging whether
  it is inside the window. For prices quoted several times, report the latest reading before the
  cutoff with its time.
  "Analysts said" / "reports suggest" without a name is not allowed.
- Earnings: actual vs consensus for EPS and revenue; guidance old → new.
- Analyst actions: firm, rating old → new, PT old → new.
- Mark unconfirmed items (people familiar, leaks, social media, M&A speculation) with [rumor]. A
  Bloomberg/Reuters/WSJ report citing sources is still reportable: state it and mark [report].
- If one event moved several stocks, name every stock and its move in the same bullet.
- Only facts published in the window. Older background only if it is the direct cause of a move in
  the window, labelled with its date.
- Do not interpret price action. Do not write "strong", "beat expectations", "investors cheered",
  "remains", "continues to", "well-positioned", "tailwinds". Write the number.
- Do not write bullets about what you could not find. Omit the topic instead.
- Do not drop facts to save space.
content:
## **SK Hynix / Solidigm** — Chip Equipment · Fab & Foundry
- Solidigm, SK Hynix’s U.S. subsidiary, sought Washington approval to ship additional U.S.-made chipmaking equipment to its Dalian, China facility; the request was linked to SK Hynix’s proposed new U.S. NAND factory, according to two people familiar with the matter [rumor]. (Reuters, Oct. 14; republished Oct. 15)
- Solidigm also applied for an export license for additional tools for Dalian’s Mod B facility; the Commerce Department had not issued a 2027 license for additional U.S.-made equipment and technology as of Oct. 15. (Reuters, Oct. 14; republished Oct. 15)
- SK Hynix said equipment installation at Mod B was being conducted “in close consultation with and under authorization from” the U.S. government and said it was not seeking to expand Mod B capacity. (Reuters, Oct. 14; republished Oct. 15)
- The Commerce Department revoked prior equipment-export exemptions for SK Hynix and Samsung facilities in China in 2025 and issued SK Hynix a 2026 Dalian license limiting equipment quantities; existing-facility operations could receive licenses, while capacity expansion and technology upgrades were generally excluded. (Reuters, Oct. 14; republished Oct. 15)

## **NVIDIA** — AI Compute · Semiconductors
- NVIDIA’s share of China’s data-center AI-chip market fell to 34% in the first half of 2026, while its China accelerator shipments fell 44% year over year to 678,000 units, according to IDC data reported by Reuters. (Reuters, Oct. 13; republished Oct. 15)
- Huawei shipped 572,000 AI accelerators and held 28% of China’s market in the first half of 2026; total Chinese accelerator shipments reached 2.008 million units. (Reuters, Oct. 13; republished Oct. 15)

## **U.S.–China Trade Truce** — Macro / Geopolitics
- The United States and China had reached a one-year trade truce that reduced some tariffs, removed some controls on Chinese rare-earth exports, and permitted selected Chinese firms to receive U.S. technology; the truce was described as the longest pause between the two countries in the latest trade conflict. (Economic Times, Oct. 15)
- President Donald Trump was scheduled to visit Beijing on Wednesday, with a meeting with President Xi Jinping expected to address trade tensions and U.S. restrictions on advanced-chip sales. (Economic Times, Oct. 15)

## **Iran / Russia / Venezuela Shadow Fleet** — Energy · Geopolitics
- The Trump administration was considering allowing previously sanctioned shadow-fleet vessels to transport non-sanctioned crude and petroleum products from the Persian Gulf, Iran, Russia and Venezuela, according to a U.S. official cited by Reuters [report]. (Reuters, Oct. 14; republished Oct. 15)
- Companies using the vessels would need to apply to the U.S. Treasury Department; the Energy Department said any relief would not authorize Russia to move sanctioned oil or petroleum products. (Reuters, Oct. 14; republished Oct. 15)
- Maritime sources said European Union and British insurance restrictions could limit the effect of any U.S. sanctions relief on freight rates. (Reuters, Oct. 14; republished Oct. 15)
- The reported discussions occurred as the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps intensified threats against U.S. and commercial vessels near the Strait of Hormuz. (Reuters, Oct. 14; republished Oct. 15)

## **Russia–Ukraine** — Macro / Geopolitics
- Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy told the Financial Times that Ukraine would resume strikes on Russian oil refineries after deadly Russian attacks. (Bloomberg, Oct. 15)
- Zelenskyy also accused President Donald Trump and Elon Musk of restricting Kyiv’s military access to SpaceX satellite technology. (Bloomberg, Oct. 15)
